dedupe_keys.name: global dataset of sand dam features and geographical distribution across drylands

description: Global dataset of sand dam features and geographical distribution across drylands is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Luigi Piemontese et al. Sand dams are water infrastructure, built across ephemeral sandy rivers, that increase water supply by creating an artificial sandy aquifer upstream of the dam. Despite their effectiveness and recent traction in the research and development arena, empirical data on their distribution and characteristics are scattered and largely unreported. Coverage: global; published in 2025. Formats: Image. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support water-network, drainage and hydraulic studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
